dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: #Ah, it's you, mighty {NICKNAME}! How are things going? Have you gone on another adventure? If you've heard any more amazing stories, I'm all ears!

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Tell you what, I've got a brother at the Saurian Relics Association. Name's Manqu, and man, if I told him what we saw at the Shadow Pins...

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: He'd go so green with envy, it might kill him! Gonna wait till I get back from my post to break it to him, though.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #You mean {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}? Well, all I know is that it's not a good sign.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I've heard that such marked Saurians are rejected by the Night Kingdom, the tribes, and the Saurians too. They die as they lived, alone.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #But that's just superstition. I mean, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}'s got you, right?

choices.text: About the tales of those heroes...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I'm giving it some thought. Uh, not that I'd let it affect my sentry work, though, no sir! I'm a real multitasker.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Those two from Khaenri'ah have a terrible reputation here in the tribe. All the more reason for my story to be as exciting as possible!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: So yeah, I've got to give this all the consideration it's due!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: We're an amazing bunch, we are!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Take, for example... Sanhaj from the Masters of the Night-Wind, whom all storytellers revere...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: They say he had every scroll written up to his time committed to memory, and that he was willing to go from tribe to tribe and share those tales... That said, they also say that he often tricked people, mooching food and drink off them.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Stories speak of bygone times, and they represent the wisdom of our forebears. Thus, the mere act of sharing it was seen as a selfless act, so all both loved and hated cunning Sanhaj.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Later, that tale-telling hero would himself become part of a heroic tale — a fate I doubt even he ever envisioned... But yeah. Sanhaj was an amazing storyteller.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Still, the characters in his tales were all tribal warriors of a sort, but in mine, we'll also include a golden-haired outlander, a silver-haired fairy, and a little Saurian with a red scarf.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: So, if only in terms of the variety of main characters, I'm the winner here!

choices.text: See you! Guard your post well!
